chunks.text: 50-year-old female, Associate Professional or Technician, resident of Woodlands, Singapore.
Discontinued Simvastatin due to muscle pain (2019)
General Anesthesia with Laryngeal Mask Airway (LMA)

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr./Ms. [Patient's Name]. I'm going to be your anesthesiologist for your laparoscopic cholecystectomy today. I'd like to go through a few questions to make sure we're all set for your surgery.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Morning, Doctor. I'm ready when you are.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Can you tell me a bit about your medical history? We know you have hypertension, diabetes, and obesity, but are there any other conditions we should know about?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all. My blood pressure and sugar have been under control, lah. I take my meds regularly.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Let's go through your medications. You're on Metformin, Lisinopril, Atorvastatin, and you were on Ranitidine but it's stopped now, correct?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, that's right. I stopped the Ranitidine a few weeks ago as instructed.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Now, regarding allergies. Your records say 'no known allergies', but I understand you mentioned a reaction to Penicillin before. Can you tell me more about that?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh yes, I had a rash when I took Penicillin once, so I avoid that now.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Have you ever had any adverse reactions to other antibiotics, like Cephalosporins, for example?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Actually, yes. I took a Cephalosporin once before, and I felt really nauseous and vomited. It was pretty bad, so I told my doctor not to give me that again.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. It's very important we know about all reactions. We'll make sure to note that allergy clearly in your chart.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Thanks, Doctor. I didn't think it was that important, but I guess it is.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Absolutely. Allergic reactions, even if not life-threatening, help us choose safer alternatives. Now, have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, this is my first time. I'm a bit nervous, to be honest.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's completely normal. We'll be with you every step of the way. Just to confirm, you've had nothing to eat or drink since midnight, as instructed?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I followed the fasting instructions. Nothing since last night.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. And how are you feeling today? Any chest pain, shortness of breath, or other symptoms we should know about?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I'm feeling fine. Just a bit anxious about the surgery, but otherwise okay.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for going through all that with me. We'll be using general anesthesia with a Laryngeal Mask Airway for your surgery. I'll explain the plan in a moment, but first, do you have any questions for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think you've covered everything. I'm ready.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] LMA size four in place, good seal, capnograph waveform confirmed

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] 18 gauge intravenous access, one liter normal saline running

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] mean arterial pressure dropped to fifty five, atropine point five milligrams given

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:35] rocuronium twenty milligrams for muscle relaxation

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:50] desaturation to eighty nine percent, increased FiO2 to one point zero

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Eh, a bit sore, but I think it's manageable. My tummy is aching a little.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Okay, can you tell me your pain level on a scale from 1 to 10?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe around 4 or 5? It's not too bad, but I can feel it.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright, and are you feeling any nausea or dizziness right now?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, not really. I feel a bit thirsty, but no vomiting or anything.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. How's your breathing? Any discomfort or tightness in your chest?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I'm breathing fine. My throat is a bit sore from the tube, I think.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That can happen with the LMA. Do you remember anything from the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I don't remember anything. I just woke up here.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's normal under general anesthesia. Given your diabetes and high blood pressure, are you having any chest pain, shortness of breath, or unusual symptoms?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, nothing like that. Just the usual tiredness and a bit of pain.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. We'll keep monitoring your vitals and manage your pain and blood sugar closely. Let the nurse know if you need anything.

50-year-old female post-laparoscopic cholecystectomy under general anesthesia with LMA.

Patient has controlled hypertension (Lisinopril 10mg once daily) and diabetes (Metformin 500mg twice daily), with a history of obesity and a desaturation event during surgery requiring increased FiO2 to 1.0.

Anticipated concerns include PONV due to history of nausea and vomiting with Cephalosporin, potential for difficult ventilation or desaturation events due to obesity, need for glycemic control monitoring, watch for hypotension due to Lisinopril and intra-op medications, and management of increased post-operative pain due to obesity and laparoscopic surgery.

Monitor for PONV, maintain vigilance for airway and desaturation issues, closely monitor blood glucose levels, watch for signs of hypotension, and ensure adequate analgesia management. Be prepared for potential airway re-emergence issues.
Patient reports abdominal pain rated 4-5 on a scale of 1-10, described as manageable.
Patient denies nausea or vomiting post-operatively.
Patient reports sore throat, likely due to Laryngeal Mask Airway (LMA) use.
Patient denies breathing difficulties or chest discomfort post-operatively.
Patient has no recall of the surgical procedure, consistent with general anesthesia.
Patient denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or unusual symptoms related to diabetes and hypertension.
Patient's vital signs will be monitored closely, with attention to blood sugar and pain management.
Intraoperative mean arterial pressure dropped to 55 mmHg, requiring atropine 0.5 mg.
Intraoperative desaturation to 89% occurred, managed by increasing FiO2 to 1.0.
